question: On the fixed previously viewed H128 workload, does commit-time direct admission retain more useful peer service at acceptable full-request cost than the same selected/eager backend with recheck disabled?
mechanism: Same staged store/prepare, next-step commit and victim selection. Only commit_recheck False/True changes. On bypasses planned victim preemption when current complete-history KV, slots, ownership and native zero inflight reservation permit direct target admission.
qualification_requirement: Original diagnostic must qualify a real direct native admission, matching completed load or positive scheduled work, subsequent new target output, target completion, and no same-step preemption of planned victim. No direct action stops this extension.
input: Same qualified H128 input and warmups; all 25 payload bytes retained in two new package identities to respect launch-once markers. No seed, arrival, threshold or prompt changes.
execution: Each adjacent pair is one independently completed shared-lock unit, 900s/cell and 3200s/unit maximum; release and inspect full results before next unit. Block2 is a predeclared order check, not conditional on a favorable Block1. Runtime/qualification/archive failure stops subsequent execution pending source localization. No automatic lock retries.

comparison.primary_service_goal: Lower maximum across per-request maximum observed generation gaps in each block while both efficiency budgets hold. This is a developmental experimental criterion, not production SLO or statistical confirmation.
distribution_metrics: per-request maximum gap ECDF and quantiles
online wall time and post-request drain
comparison.success_scope: Both blocks meeting the criterion is a provisional domain-specific tradeoff only. Report block disagreement and all action counts. Two blocks cannot establish statistical stability or new-data generalization.

stopping_rules: Do not add T/Q, seeds, loads or repeats to rescue failure.
Zero direct actions in performance is retained as an action-availability boundary; no input tuning.
No original per-action common-state counterfactual is available: separate policy trajectories support paired policy-level comparison only.
Natural sequence/workload changes prohibit equal-work speedup claims; no tensor equality or quality assertion.
Defensive reservation check is not an algorithm contribution; H1 itself is a simple direct-if-feasible rule.
future_gate: Only a material credible positive tradeoff would justify new held-out data, quality/correctness expansion and action-level prior-art audit. Otherwise preserve specific failure and investigate a newly evidenced residual, without claiming full-paper readiness.
